wall_stone.label: Stone wall
wall_stone.note: the village's stone wall, built a segment at a time like the wooden walls; shown and buildable only while Free building is on (as the round stone wall), its cost the placeholder and Primary's default, never charged while Free building is on (Michael, 2026-10-29: straight stone walls were missing from the build menu; the castle's gates and battlements stamp over it)

round_stone.label: Round stone wall
round_stone.note: docs/50: a round room, 5 or 7 across, by a drag from one corner of its square; stone only, shown and buildable only while Free building is on (Michael, 2026-10-27: "A few on the map, buildable by dev settings, otherwise not in the game yet until we settle on cost, etc."); its cost is per edge of the outline (40 stone at 5, 56 at 7), a placeholder and Primary's default, never charged since Free building waives it; the seconds the builder's default (two fifths more at 7)

fireplace.label: Fireplace
fireplace.note: the Fireplace (Michael, 2026-10-26, the fire rulings under Round rooms: a spec; it replaced the generated hearth): the drawn fireplace, two tiles along a flat wall indoors, its facing from the wall it backs onto (src/setdown.js fitFor); a switch (docs/43 section 3), out when built; cooks; never moved; taken apart out for half its stone; no tool (the builder's default, as the hearth's was)

fire_pit.label: Fire pit
fire_pit.note: the fire pit (Michael, 2026-10-26, the fire rulings): 2 by 2 on open ground, indoors or out, never on water (roads are fine), clear of a door's two tiles; a switch, out when built; cooks; never moved; taken apart out for half its stone; the cost and the seconds Primary's and the builder's defaults; no tool, as the Fireplace

feed_trough.label: Feeding trough
feed_trough.note: docs/45 section 3: a feeding trough (not the water trough) in a pen, filled with grain, vegetables, or hay; built from the palette, planks (Primary's default)

floor_wood.label: Plank floor
floor_wood.note: docs/49 section 5 (Michael, 2026-10-27, 02 "Floors are built a tile at a time, with no physics"): a tile at a time, by a drag for a rectangle; on the ground over the floor there (kept, and put back when it is taken up), on a storey wherever it touches a floor already walkable there; shown and buildable only while Free building is on until the floors are costed (Primary's default, as the round stone wall); 1 plank a tile, a placeholder and Primary's default, never charged while Free building is on; the seconds a tile the builder's default

floor_stone.label: Stone floor
floor_stone.note: as the Plank floor, in the stone floor the map already draws; 1 stone a tile (Primary's default)

stair_wood.label: Wood stair
stair_wood.note: docs/49 section 5: a stair three tiles long from the tile under the cursor, climbing on away from the player, its landing's planks laid on the storey above (one of its planks); north and west only for now (Primary's default: "Stairs climb away from the camera", Michael to confirm); the drawn stair (art round 8); never taken apart (ruled); Free building only for now; the cost docs/49 section 5's default, never charged while Free building is on; the seconds the builder's default

stair_stone.label: Stone stair
stair_stone.note: as the Wood stair, in stone (9 stone and a plank, docs/49 section 5's default); its landing a stone floor

terrain_grass.label: Grass
terrain_grass.note: Terrain tab (Michael, 2026-10-28: split the build menu in two, Build and Terrain): paints the ground's floor outright by a drag (up to 24 tiles a side), a tile at a time, no cost and no `built` record, so there is nothing to take apart; grass, the ground's own: painted over dirt, cobble, or water it blends with the dirt and cobble round it as the authored grass does; ground only, Free building only; `seconds` 0 (instant) and `reach` 12 tiles are a world-editing tool's, Primary's defaults

terrain_dirt.label: Dirt
terrain_dirt.note: Terrain tab (Michael, 2026-10-28: split the build menu in two, Build and Terrain): paints the ground's floor outright by a drag (up to 24 tiles a side), a tile at a time, no cost and no `built` record, so there is nothing to take apart; bare earth: its edge against grass is ragged, as the valley's paths are (the ground bake keys it off the tile's floor, not off who made it); ground only, Free building only; `seconds` 0 (instant) and `reach` 12 tiles are a world-editing tool's, Primary's defaults

terrain_cobble.label: Cobblestone
terrain_cobble.note: Terrain tab (Michael, 2026-10-28: split the build menu in two, Build and Terrain): paints the ground's floor outright by a drag (up to 24 tiles a side), a tile at a time, no cost and no `built` record, so there is nothing to take apart; cobbles, inside a dirt verge as the valley's roads are; ground only, Free building only; `seconds` 0 (instant) and `reach` 12 tiles are a world-editing tool's, Primary's defaults

terrain_randomspawn.label: Random spawn
terrain_randomspawn.note: Terrain tab (Michael, 2026-10-28: split the build menu in two, Build and Terrain): paints the ground's floor outright by a drag (up to 24 tiles a side), a tile at a time, no cost and no `built` record, so there is nothing to take apart; bubblegum pink, on purpose: a tag for the hand-built map (Michael, 2026-10-28, who swapped its meaning the same day from No random spawn): it marks a tile where random things CAN spawn (trees, the dead, whatever the map's scatter and spawn rules later place) and does nothing else yet: nothing reads it; ground only, Free building only; `seconds` 0 (instant) and `reach` 12 tiles are a world-editing tool's, Primary's defaults

terrain_water_shallow.label: Shallow water
terrain_water_shallow.note: Terrain tab (Michael, 2026-10-28: split the build menu in two, Build and Terrain): paints the ground's floor outright by a drag (up to 24 tiles a side), a tile at a time, no cost and no `built` record, so there is nothing to take apart; a ford: walked at half speed, drunk from; a hard-edged tile like the valley's shallows; ground only, Free building only; `seconds` 0 (instant) and `reach` 12 tiles are a world-editing tool's, Primary's defaults

terrain_water.label: Water
terrain_water.note: Terrain tab (Michael, 2026-10-28: split the build menu in two, Build and Terrain): paints the ground's floor outright by a drag (up to 24 tiles a side), a tile at a time, no cost and no `built` record, so there is nothing to take apart; wholly water: no one walks it (a tile under a body, a prop, a rug, an item, or a wall edge is refused); its edge against grass and dirt is ragged, as the river's; ground only, Free building only; `seconds` 0 (instant) and `reach` 12 tiles are a world-editing tool's, Primary's defaults

wall_cliff.label: Cliff wall
wall_cliff.note: art round 10 (Michael, 2026-10-28: "wire that cliff art for testing"): a cliff face on a tile edge, 96 tall, bare rock; blocks bodies and sight as stone; no door or window stamped in it, nothing hung on it, taken apart only while Free building is on; a cliff-top floor laid on the storey above it makes it a hill's edge (render/walls.js draws its lip, its back, and the corner pieces); Free building only, for experimenting; the cost a placeholder (a stone, as the stone floor), never charged while Free building is on

wall_cliff_grass.label: Grassy cliff wall
wall_cliff_grass.note: as the Cliff wall, its turf rolled over the lip (art round 10)

floor_cliff_top.label: Cliff top
floor_cliff_top.note: art round 10: bare rock with scree and lichen, laid as the stone floor (docs/49 section 5: a tile at a time, on the ground or upstairs, no physics); over cliff walls it is a hill's top; Free building only; the cost the stone floor's, a placeholder

floor_cliff_grass.label: Grassy cliff top
floor_cliff_grass.note: as the Cliff top, turf with a rock nub now and then (art round 10)

stair_ramp_stone.label: Stone ramp
stair_ramp_stone.note: art round 10: a sloped slab of the cliff's rock climbing one storey over three tiles, north or west, built as a stair (docs/49 section 5) and walked at 32 px a tile with no treads (map.riseOn); its landing a cliff top (its definition's `landing`) unless a floor is laid there already; it lays its own square side walls (wall_ramp_side) on the ground under its landing, so it keeps its whole solid shape; never taken apart, as a stair; Free building only; placed at once and free like the Terrain tab's other pieces (Michael, 2026-10-29: "make ramps build immediately for now just for building"): no bar, no cost, no tool

gate_stone_2.label: Stone gate (2 wide)
gate_stone_2.hint: Click, then click a plain stone wall: a 2-tile gate with a portcullis replaces the wall at once; E opens and shuts it
gate_stone_2.note: docs/09 (Michael, 2026-10-29: "Free building only", "Agreed, for now"): a 2-tile castle gate stamped over 2 plain stone wall edges in a row, shut, placed at once and free as the Stone ramp is (no bar, no cost, no tool); E opens and shuts it like a door; taking it apart puts the plain wall back

gate_stone_3.label: Stone gate (3 wide)
gate_stone_3.hint: Click, then click a plain stone wall: a 3-tile gate with a portcullis replaces the wall at once; E opens and shuts it
gate_stone_3.note: docs/09 (Michael, 2026-10-29: "Free building only", "Agreed, for now"): a 3-tile castle gate stamped over 3 plain stone wall edges in a row, shut, placed at once and free as the Stone ramp is (no bar, no cost, no tool); E opens and shuts it like a door; taking it apart puts the plain wall back

battlement_stone.label: Battlement
battlement_stone.hint: Click an edge of a wall walk's floor, upstairs: a parapet with merlons stands on the edge outside the walkway, which stays whole
battlement_stone.note: docs/09 (Michael, 2026-10-29: "design me a short stone wall with these merlons ... make sure the whole of the battlement sits outside the walkway", art round 13 approved): a castle's parapet, a short stone wall wholly on the outside of a tile edge of a floor on layer 1 or higher, with the walkway's floor on one side of the edge and none on the other (src/battlements.js); its side, its variant, and its corners and ends are read from the floors and the neighbouring edges, never saved; sight and light pass it, bodies and the dead do not, and the dead cannot strike it down; placed at once and free as the Stone ramp is (no bar, no cost, no tool); Free building only
